channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Hold Recruitment Agencies Accountable for Foreign Students' Welfare
item.description: Kyrgyzstan will require recruitment agencies to support foreign students throughout their entire study period. This measure aims to address issues with unscrupulous intermediaries who previously abandoned students after enrollment. New contracts will ensure agencies assist students until graduation, with the state enterprise 'Center for Admission of Foreign Students' overseeing compliance.

item.title: Glencore Nears Deal to Sell Stake in Kazakhstan's Kazzinc
item.description: Swiss company Glencore is in final negotiations to sell its controlling stake in Kazakh zinc and gold producer Kazzinc to a local investor. A decision is expected within two months. Analysts estimate the deal could be worth up to $5 billion. Previous reports indicated negotiations with businessman Shakhmuart Mutalip.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Aims to Attract European Students to Its Universities
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to expand its reach for international students by actively promoting its universities in European countries. Currently, the majority of foreign students come from India and Pakistan. The Ministry of Science, Higher Education, and Innovation aims to enter new educational markets, including Europe, with plans for international exhibition participation and potential overseas student reception centers.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Increase Minimum Wage to 110,000 Tenge from Next Year
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has instructed the government to raise the minimum wage from 85,000 to 110,000 tenge, effective January 1 next year. This increase is expected to boost the income of 1.8 million people, including over 370,000 public sector employees. Additionally, doctors' salaries will be raised.

item.title: Kazakh Lawmaker Advises Using Smartphones for Additional Income
item.description: Kazakh Parliament member Askhat Aimagambetov suggested that smartphones should be used by citizens to generate additional income, rather than for leisure. He proposed enabling farmers to sell produce directly through marketplaces and allowing citizens to invest in businesses or company shares via tokenization. President Tokayev also previously urged the use of phones for work and earning.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Launch Nationwide Renovation of Communal Networks
item.description: Following the Ekibastuz incident, Kazakhstan plans a large-scale "People's Construction" project focused on renovating communal networks, including heating and water systems. The goal is to ensure basic living conditions in all homes. The speed of repairs will depend on the readiness of documentation and the efficiency of local administrations, according to Deputy Serik Yegizbayev.

item.title: Six Found Dead in Tashkent Construction Site Suspected of Gas Poisoning
item.description: Six people were found dead on October 25 at a private construction site in Tashkent's Mirzo Ulugbek district, likely due to carbon monoxide poisoning. Two others were hospitalized in serious condition. An investigation has been launched into potential safety violations.

item.title: Iran's President Tells Putin Middle East Can Solve Problems Without US Involvement
item.description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian informed Russian President Vladimir Putin that Middle Eastern nations can resolve regional issues independently of the United States. The leaders pledged to enhance cooperation, noting growing trade and mutual support amid regional tensions and US sanctions.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan discusses aviation development with international consultants
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's First Deputy Head of the Cabinet of Ministers met with James Hogan, chairman of Knighthood Global, to discuss civil aviation cooperation. Topics included expanding international air travel, modernizing airport infrastructure, and enhancing the competitiveness of Kyrgyz airlines. No specific agreements were announced.

item.title: Kazakh MP explains who may face higher taxes after proposed increase
item.description: Kazakhstan's Kurultai deputy, Askhat Aimagambetov, stated that proposed tax increases would target very wealthy individuals, not the middle class, aligning with a global trend towards progressive taxation. The government is discussing specific details for potential amendments to the Tax Code, following President Tokayev's initiative.

item.title: Cyclone 'Arnabb' Hits India's Andhra Pradesh Coast, 89,000 Evacuated
item.description: Cyclone 'Arnabb' made landfall on the coast of India's Andhra Pradesh state, prompting authorities to evacuate 89,000 people from vulnerable areas. Winds reached speeds of up to 185 km/h, causing heavy rainfall and significant damage in coastal districts. No casualties have been reported yet.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Increase Salaries for Primary Healthcare Doctors by Up to 40% by 2027
item.description: Starting January 1st, the salaries of primary healthcare doctors in Kazakhstan will increase by up to 40%. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev announced this during his address to the nation, stating the raise will depend on their continuous work experience. This measure aims to improve the compensation for frontline medical professionals.

item.title: Kazakh MP Aidos Sarym Comments on Taxing Wealthy Individuals
item.description: Kazakh Member of Parliament Aidos Sarym shared his views on President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's proposal to tax wealthy Kazakhs. Sarym believes a proper culture regarding wealth needs to be established, suggesting that the lifestyle and actions of the wealthy significantly impact public sentiment. He noted that MPs primarily belong to the middle class.

item.title: Kazakh MP Explains AI Market Downturn and Kazakhstan's Digitalization Path
item.description: Kazakhstan's Kurultai deputy Yerlan Sairo advises against abandoning AI development despite a recent market downturn. He notes that while the AI market may be overheated, digitalization and AI are key trends for the 21st century. Sairo emphasizes Kazakhstan's need to align with global scientific and technological progress and supports the president's digital society initiative.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Increase Salaries for General Practitioners Based on Service Length
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Health plans to introduce additional payments for general practitioners starting January 1, potentially increasing salaries by up to 50% based on years of service. The aim is to enhance the quality and accessibility of primary care. In rural areas, salaries for experienced doctors could rise from 534,000 to 760,000 tenge.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Build Three Major Children's Medical Centers in Astana and Almaty
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to construct 20 new maternal and child healthcare facilities by 2029, including three major republican children's medical centers in Astana and Almaty. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev announced the ambitious project, emphasizing the need for healthcare infrastructure development due to the country's rapid population growth. The new centers will enhance diagnostic and treatment capabilities for complex pediatric cases.

item.title: Uzbekistan Offers Tax and Customs Benefits for Tourism Development Around Reservoirs
item.description: Uzbekistan has introduced measures to regulate the use and ensure the safety of reservoirs and adjacent areas. Entrepreneurs organizing tourism services in these locations will receive benefits until October 1, 2029. These include reduced rates for land and property taxes and deferred customs payments for imported equipment. Strict safety and environmental requirements will also apply.

item.title: Uzbekistan Pays Compensation to Families Affected by Dok-1 Max and Ambronol
item.description: Following President's directive, compensation payments have been made to families affected by the drugs Dok-1 Max and Ambronol. The Tashkent City Court had initially paid only 20% of the compensation owed to 90 victims. Additional funds were allocated from the budget, resulting in 72.2 billion soms paid to families of deceased children and 7.8 billion soms to families of those undergoing treatment.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Energy Sector Faces Critical Juncture Amidst Industry Challenges
item.description: Kazakhstan's oil and gas sector is at a critical point, facing numerous challenges despite a recent industry event suggesting otherwise. Discussions at the 30th Kazakhstan Oil & Gas Exhibition (KIOGE) in Almaty highlighted issues of partnership deficits and infrastructure difficulties. Experts noted unique resource potential but pointed to regulatory and fiscal inconsistencies hindering development.

item.title: Tashkent Residents Advised to Keep Windows Closed Due to Smog
item.description: Tashkent's air quality is expected to be at an "unhealthy" level on October 28 due to smog. The National Committee on Ecology and Climate Change recommends sensitive groups, including children and the elderly, to limit outdoor activity. When going out, masks should be worn, and windows should be kept closed indoors, especially in the evening and at night.

item.title: Uzbekistan Pays $6.6 Million to Families of "Dok-1 Max" Syrup Victims
item.description: Families of victims of the "Dok-1 Max" syrup in Uzbekistan have received $6.6 million (80 billion soums). Payments include 72 billion soums for 72 deceased children and 7.8 billion soums for 16 children undergoing treatment. Compensation has been provided to 88 out of 90 families awarded by court. The remaining funds will be disbursed after resolving technical banking issues.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan amends law to count national team service as work experience
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has amended its law on physical culture and sports to include time spent in national teams as part of an athlete's work experience. The change, announced by the Director of the State Agency for Physical Culture and Sports, aims to support athletes after their careers end. Starting at age 18, service in the national team will now count towards an athlete's work record, facilitating their professional adaptation and social protection.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan sports federations to undergo re-accreditation and performance review
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to tighten requirements for sports federations and revise state funding approaches. Organizations failing to show results may face reduced support, according to the Director of the State Agency for Physical Culture and Sports. Changes to legislation mandate re-accreditation, with increased control over their activities and performance evaluation. Federations will be assessed on infrastructure, coaches, athletes, and regional presence.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Raise Minimum Wage to 110,000 Tenge from 2027
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has instructed the government to increase the minimum wage from 85,000 to 110,000 tenge starting January 1, 2027. This measure is expected to boost the income of 1.8 million people, including over 370,000 public sector employees.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans to Abolish Regions and Districts, Creating 20 Large Administrative Okrugs
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is planning a second phase of administrative-territorial reform, which includes abolishing all existing regions and districts to establish 20 new, larger administrative okrugs. President Sadyr Japarov stated that this reform aims to simplify governance, with a pilot project for one okrug to be implemented first. The success will be measured by the okrug's ability to become self-sufficient and not rely on state subsidies.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Build Major Chemical Complex in Mangystau Region
item.description: A significant chemical complex is planned for construction in Kazakhstan's Mangystau region, with an estimated cost of $1.59 billion. The facility is slated for operation by 2030 and will produce ammonia, urea, and ammonium nitrate. The project is expected to create 700 jobs and represents a major industrial development for the region.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Prosecutor General's Office: Detainee Should File Torture Complaint
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Deputy Prosecutor General stated that activist Askat Zhetigen should file a formal complaint regarding his allegations of torture while in custody. The office emphasized that official statements on social media are insufficient for initiating a criminal case, and an investigation requires a formal written application.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Increase Minimum Wage to 110,000 Tenge and Boost Healthcare Worker Pay
item.description: Starting January 1, 2027, Kazakhstan will raise its minimum wage to 110,000 tenge and increase salaries for primary healthcare specialists by up to 40%. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev announced these measures, aimed at modernizing primary healthcare and benefiting over 1.8 million citizens, including 370,000 in the public sector.

item.title: Kazakh President Orders Comprehensive Reform of State Governance System
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has ordered a comprehensive reform of the state governance system, starting from the government down to village akims. He emphasized the need for institutions to operate efficiently in the digital age, utilizing artificial intelligence and reducing bureaucracy.

item.title: Kazakh President Prioritizes Teacher Support, Aims to Reduce Workload and Enhance Respect
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev emphasized that educational reforms should ease teachers' burdens and reduce excessive workload, addressing issues like excessive paperwork and digital reporting. He also highlighted the need to protect teachers from disrespect and violence from students and administrative pressure.

item.title: Uzbekistan Completes Compensation Payments for 'Dok-1 Maks' Drug Victims
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Health announced that the remaining 65.2 billion soums in compensation for victims of 'Dok-1 Maks' and 'Ambronol' have been paid from the state budget. A total of 82 billion soums was ordered for 90 victims, with 16.8 billion paid previously. Now, 88 victims have received 80 billion soums.

item.title: Taliban Claim Nearly 4,000 People Returned to Afghanistan by Force in Six Days
item.description: The Taliban announced that 3,850 people in 819 families have been forcibly returned to Afghanistan over the past six days. Deputy spokesperson Hamdullah Fitrat stated that returns occurred through Torkham, Silk Bridge, Spin Boldak, and Islam Qala crossings. The UN reported 4.9 million migrant returns in three years, straining services.

item.title: Kazakhstan's President Tokayev Outlines Ninth Address Focused on National Development
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev announced a large-scale construction plan for Kazakhstan, allocating 6.5 trillion tenge from the National Fund for infrastructure development. He also proposed raising the minimum wage to 110,000 tenge, eliminating energy shortages by 2029, and reforming public administration. The initiative is termed 'People's Construction'.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Outlines Economic Priorities in National Address
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev of Kazakhstan has outlined key economic tasks in his address to the nation. Priorities include tax policy, water management, logistics, digitalization, and social policy. Tokayev emphasized large-scale infrastructure renewal, including roads, industrial facilities, railways, and social buildings, aiming for a construction boom across all regions.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Fully Reform State Governance System by June 2027
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has ordered the preparation of a plan to reform Kazakhstan's state governance system, due by June 1, 2027. The administration will also develop a long-term development document with research institutions. Reforms aim to increase efficiency across all government levels, integrate artificial intelligence, and reduce bureaucracy. New ethical principles for civil servants are also proposed.

item.title: Dushanbe Hosts Meeting on Leveraging Interpol's Capabilities Against Transnational Crime
item.description: Officials from Tajikistan's Interpol bureau and the EU's Border Management Programme in Central Asia (BOMCA) met in Dushanbe on October 26, 2026. The discussions focused on enhancing cooperation, improving information exchange, and utilizing Interpol's resources to combat transnational crime. The meeting aimed to identify priority areas for future collaboration and strengthen joint law enforcement capabilities.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Offer Monthly Bonuses Up to $4,100 for Returning Doctors
item.description: Uzbekistan's President announced new support measures for medical professionals, including monthly bonuses up to 50 million soums (approx. $4,100) for expatriate doctors with foreign experience. They are guaranteed employment and the ability to form their own teams. The state will also allocate 50 billion soums for mortgage down payments for experienced local medical staff.

item.title: US President Trump Suggests Potential Meeting with Putin and Zelensky
item.description: US President Donald Trump indicated a possible upcoming meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. Trump stated the US is making significant progress regarding Russia and Ukraine, though details on the format remain unspecified. Both Moscow and Kyiv have yet to comment.

item.title: Taliban Mortar Fire Kills Civilian in Pakistan's South Waziristan
item.description: Taliban forces fired mortar rounds into Pakistan's Lower South Waziristan district, killing one civilian and wounding five others on October 27. The mortar struck civilian homes and shops. Pakistani forces returned fire, reportedly destroying several Taliban border posts. The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa governor condemned the 'unprovoked aggression'.

item.title: Trump Suggests Potential Meeting with Putin and Zelensky for Peace Talks
item.description: US President Donald Trump has indicated the possibility of an imminent meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky to advance peace negotiations. Trump expressed hope for significant progress during potential talks, which come amid intensified diplomatic efforts to resolve the conflict in Ukraine.
